notes:
1. Basic Facts
  • Peninsular rivers drain the ancient plateau region of India.
  • Most originate in the Western Ghats, Central Highlands or adjoining plateau regions.
  • Their valleys are generally broader and shallower than Himalayan river valleys.
  • Their courses are relatively more fixed because the Peninsular Plateau is geologically old and stable.
  • Most depend heavily on monsoon rainfall.
  • Therefore, their seasonal variation in discharge is generally greater than that of Himalayan rivers.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Peninsular Rivers → Old Courses + Fixed Valleys + Monsoon-Dependent

2. Major Peninsular River Systems

Important peninsular rivers include:

  • Mahanadi.
  • Godavari.
  • Krishna.
  • Kaveri.
  • Narmada.
  • Tapi.
  • Pennar.
  • Subarnarekha.
  • Brahmani.
  • Baitarani.
  • Sabarmati.
  • Luni.
  • Several short west-flowing rivers.
3. East-Flowing vs West-Flowing Rivers

Most major Peninsular rivers flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal.

Important east-flowing rivers include:

  • Mahanadi.
  • Godavari.
  • Krishna.
  • Kaveri.
  • Pennar.

Important west-flowing rivers include:

  • Narmada.
  • Tapi.
  • Mahi.
  • Sabarmati.
  • Numerous short Western Ghats rivers.
📌 Must-Memorise

Most Peninsular Rivers → East-Flowing

4. Why Most Peninsular Rivers Flow East
  • The Peninsular Plateau generally slopes from west to east.
  • The Western Ghats form the highest western edge.
  • Rivers therefore commonly flow eastward across the plateau toward the Bay of Bengal.
5. East-Flowing River Characteristics

East-flowing rivers generally:

  • Have longer courses.
  • Drain larger basins.
  • Carry significant sediment.
  • Form large deltas near the Bay of Bengal.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

East-Flowing Peninsular Rivers → Deltas

6. West-Flowing River Characteristics

West-flowing rivers generally:

  • Have shorter courses where they originate in the Western Ghats.
  • Flow down steep gradients.
  • Form estuaries more commonly than large deltas.
  • Reach the Arabian Sea.
7. Narmada and Tapi — Major Exceptions
  • Narmada and Tapi are major long west-flowing Peninsular rivers.
  • Both flow through structurally controlled valleys.
  • They drain into the Arabian Sea.
📌 Must-Memorise

Narmada + Tapi → West-Flowing → Arabian Sea

8. Rift Valley Rivers
  • Narmada and Tapi flow through rift valleys.
  • Rift valleys form due to faulting of the Earth's crust.
  • These rivers flow between major structural highlands.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Rift Valley Rivers → Narmada + Tapi

9. Narmada River — Overview
  • Narmada is one of India's major west-flowing rivers.
  • It originates near Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh.
  • It flows westward between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.
  • It drains into the Gulf of Khambhat in the Arabian Sea.
📌 Must-Memorise

Narmada → Amarkantak → Rift Valley → Arabian Sea

10. Narmada Source
  • Narmada originates from the Amarkantak Plateau region.
  • Amarkantak lies in Madhya Pradesh.
  • The source region is associated with the Maikal Hills.
11. Narmada Valley
  • Narmada flows through a faulted structural valley.
  • Vindhya Range lies mainly to its north.
  • Satpura Range lies mainly to its south.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Narmada → Between Vindhya and Satpura

12. Narmada Drainage Direction
  • Narmada flows from east to west.
  • This is opposite to the general eastward drainage direction of most large Peninsular rivers.
13. Narmada Estuary
  • Narmada enters the Arabian Sea through an estuary.
  • It does not form a large delta.
  • Strong tidal action and structural conditions favour an estuarine mouth.
14. Major Tributaries of Narmada

Important tributaries include:

  • Tawa.
  • Hiran.
  • Shakkar.
  • Dudhi.
  • Banjar.
15. Tawa River
  • Tawa is one of the important tributaries of Narmada.
  • Tawa Dam is built on this river in Madhya Pradesh.
16. Marble Rocks
  • Narmada flows through the famous Marble Rocks near Bhedaghat in Madhya Pradesh.
  • The river has cut a gorge through marble formations.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Bhedaghat → Narmada → Marble Rocks

17. Dhuandhar Falls
  • Dhuandhar Falls lies on the Narmada River near Bhedaghat.
  • It is an important waterfall of Madhya Pradesh.
📌 Must-Memorise

Dhuandhar Falls → Narmada

18. Sardar Sarovar Dam
  • Sardar Sarovar Dam is built on the Narmada River.
  • It is located in Gujarat.
  • The project supports irrigation, drinking water and hydroelectric power.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Sardar Sarovar → Narmada → Gujarat

19. Indira Sagar Project
  • Indira Sagar Dam is built on Narmada in Madhya Pradesh.
  • It is an important multipurpose project.
20. Omkareshwar Project
  • Omkareshwar Dam is built on Narmada in Madhya Pradesh.
  • It is associated with irrigation and hydropower.
21. Tapi River — Overview
  • Tapi, also called Tapti, is another major west-flowing river.
  • It originates near Multai in Madhya Pradesh.
  • It flows westward through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat.
  • It enters the Arabian Sea through the Gulf of Khambhat.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tapi → Multai → Westward → Gulf of Khambhat

22. Tapi Valley
  • Tapi flows through a structurally controlled valley.
  • It lies south of the Satpura Range.
  • Like Narmada, it is associated with rift-valley drainage.
23. Major Tapi Tributaries

Important tributaries include:

  • Purna.
  • Girna.
  • Panjhra.
  • Waghur.
  • Aner.
24. Ukai Dam
  • Ukai Dam is built on the Tapi River in Gujarat.
  • It supports irrigation, flood control and hydropower.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Ukai Dam → Tapi

25. Surat and Tapi
  • Surat lies on the Tapi River in Gujarat.
  • Tapi reaches the Arabian Sea near Surat.
26. Mahi River
  • Mahi originates in Madhya Pradesh.
  • It flows through Rajasthan and Gujarat.
  • It drains into the Gulf of Khambhat.
  • It is a west-flowing river.
27. Mahi and Tropic of Cancer
  • Mahi is notable because it crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice.
📌 TNPSC Favourite

River Crossing Tropic of Cancer Twice → Mahi

28. Sabarmati River
  • Sabarmati originates in the Aravalli Hills of Rajasthan.
  • It flows through Gujarat.
  • Ahmedabad lies on the Sabarmati.
  • It drains into the Gulf of Khambhat.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Ahmedabad → Sabarmati

29. Luni River
  • Luni rises in the Aravalli region near Ajmer.
  • It flows southwestward through Rajasthan.
  • It terminates in the Rann of Kachchh region.
  • Its lower course becomes saline.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Luni → Inland/Desert Drainage

30. Short West-Flowing Rivers

Many rivers originate on the western slopes of the Western Ghats and flow directly into the Arabian Sea.

Examples include:

  • Mandovi.
  • Zuari.
  • Kali.
  • Sharavathi.
  • Netravati.
  • Periyar.
  • Bharathapuzha.
31. Sharavathi River
  • Sharavathi flows in Karnataka.
  • It originates in the Western Ghats.
  • Jog Falls is located on this river.
  • It drains into the Arabian Sea.
📌 Must-Memorise

Jog Falls → Sharavathi

32. Jog Falls
  • Jog Falls is one of India's famous waterfalls.
  • It is located in Karnataka.
  • It is formed by the Sharavathi River.
33. Mandovi River
  • Mandovi is an important river of Goa.
  • It drains into the Arabian Sea.
  • It forms part of Goa's estuarine network.
34. Zuari River
  • Zuari is another major river of Goa.
  • It forms an important estuary.
  • Mandovi and Zuari are important for Goa's coastal geography.
35. Periyar River
  • Periyar is an important river of Kerala.
  • It is one of the major rivers of the state.
  • It originates in the Western Ghats.
  • It flows westward toward the Arabian Sea.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Periyar → Kerala

36. Mullaperiyar Link
  • Mullaperiyar Dam is built across the Periyar River in Kerala.
  • Its waters are diverted eastward toward Tamil Nadu.
  • It is geographically and economically important to southern Tamil Nadu.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Mullaperiyar → Periyar → Water Diversion to Tamil Nadu

37. Bharathapuzha
  • Bharathapuzha is an important west-flowing river of Kerala.
  • It is also called Nila in Kerala.
  • It drains into the Arabian Sea.
38. Mahanadi River — Overview
  • Mahanadi is a major east-flowing river.
  • It originates in Chhattisgarh.
  • It flows through Chhattisgarh and Odisha.
  • It forms a large delta before entering the Bay of Bengal.
📌 Must-Memorise

Mahanadi → Chhattisgarh → Odisha → Bay of Bengal

39. Mahanadi Source
  • Mahanadi originates in the highlands of Chhattisgarh.
  • Its source is traditionally associated with the Sihawa Hills region.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Mahanadi Source → Sihawa Hills

40. Mahanadi Tributaries

Important tributaries include:

  • Seonath/Shivnath.
  • Hasdeo.
  • Mand.
  • Ib.
  • Ong.
  • Tel.
41. Hirakud Dam
  • Hirakud Dam is built across the Mahanadi River in Odisha.
  • It lies near Sambalpur.
  • It is one of India's major multipurpose river-valley projects.
📌 Must-Memorise

Hirakud Dam → Mahanadi → Odisha

42. Hirakud Project Uses

Major purposes include:

  • Flood control.
  • Irrigation.
  • Hydroelectricity.
43. Mahanadi Delta
  • Mahanadi forms a broad fertile delta in Odisha.
  • The region is intensively cultivated.
  • It is vulnerable to floods and cyclones.
44. Godavari River — Overview
  • Godavari is the largest Peninsular river system.
  • It is often called the Dakshin Ganga or Ganga of the South.
  • It originates near Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra.
  • It flows eastward into the Bay of Bengal.
📌 Must-Memorise

Godavari → Largest Peninsular River

Godavari = Dakshin Ganga

45. Godavari Source
  • Godavari rises near Trimbakeshwar in the Western Ghats.
  • Trimbakeshwar lies near Nashik in Maharashtra.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Godavari → Trimbakeshwar → Maharashtra

46. Godavari States

The Godavari basin extends across parts of:

  • Maharashtra.
  • Telangana.
  • Andhra Pradesh.
  • Chhattisgarh.
  • Odisha.
  • Madhya Pradesh and adjoining areas through tributary basins.
47. Major Godavari Tributaries

Important tributaries include:

  • Pravara.
  • Purna.
  • Manjira.
  • Penganga.
  • Wardha.
  • Wainganga.
  • Pranhita.
  • Indravati.
  • Sabari.
48. Pranhita River
  • Pranhita is one of the largest tributaries of Godavari.
  • It is formed by the combined drainage of major rivers including Wardha and Wainganga.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Wardha + Wainganga System → Pranhita → Godavari

49. Indravati River
  • Indravati is a major tributary of Godavari.
  • It flows through the Bastar region.
  • Chitrakote Falls is located on the Indravati.
📌 Must-Memorise

Chitrakote Falls → Indravati

50. Sabari River
  • Sabari is an important tributary of Godavari.
  • It drains parts of Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Andhra Pradesh region.
51. Manjira River
  • Manjira is an important tributary of Godavari.
  • It flows through the Deccan Plateau region.
52. Godavari Delta
  • Godavari forms a large delta in Andhra Pradesh.
  • It splits into distributaries before reaching the Bay of Bengal.
  • The delta is agriculturally productive.
53. Dowleswaram Barrage
  • The Godavari barrage near Dowleswaram in Andhra Pradesh is historically associated with irrigation development.
  • Sir Arthur Cotton played a major role in its development.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Dowleswaram → Godavari → Sir Arthur Cotton

54. Polavaram Project
  • Polavaram is a major multipurpose project on the Godavari in Andhra Pradesh.
  • It is associated with irrigation, water transfer and hydropower.
55. Jayakwadi Dam
  • Jayakwadi Dam is built on Godavari in Maharashtra.
  • It is an important irrigation project.
56. Sriram Sagar Project
  • Sriram Sagar Project is built on the Godavari in Telangana.
  • It supports irrigation.
57. Krishna River — Overview
  • Krishna is one of India's major east-flowing Peninsular rivers.
  • It originates near Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra.
  • It flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh region.
  • It drains into the Bay of Bengal.
📌 Must-Memorise

Krishna → Mahabaleshwar → Bay of Bengal

58. Krishna Source
  • Krishna originates near Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats of Maharashtra.
  • It begins close to the source regions of several other west/east-flowing rivers.
59. Major Krishna Tributaries

Important tributaries include:

  • Koyna.
  • Bhima.
  • Ghataprabha.
  • Malaprabha.
  • Tungabhadra.
  • Musi.
60. Bhima River
  • Bhima is one of Krishna's major tributaries.
  • It rises in Maharashtra.
  • It flows through Maharashtra and Karnataka.
61. Tungabhadra River
  • Tungabhadra is formed by the confluence of:
  • Tunga.
  • Bhadra.
  • These rivers originate in the Western Ghats of Karnataka.
  • Tungabhadra joins Krishna.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tungabhadra = Tunga + Bhadra

62. Tungabhadra and Vijayanagara
  • The historic city of Hampi lies on the Tungabhadra River.
  • The Vijayanagara Empire developed around this region.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Hampi → Tungabhadra

63. Musi River
  • Musi is a tributary of Krishna.
  • Hyderabad lies on the Musi River.
📌 Must-Memorise

Hyderabad → Musi

64. Koyna River
  • Koyna is an important tributary of Krishna.
  • Koyna Dam in Maharashtra is a major hydroelectric project.
65. Nagarjuna Sagar Dam
  • Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is built on the Krishna River.
  • It lies between Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
  • It is a major irrigation and hydroelectric project.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nagarjuna Sagar → Krishna

66. Srisailam Dam
  • Srisailam Dam is built on the Krishna River.
  • It lies on the Andhra Pradesh-Telangana border region.
  • It is important for hydropower and irrigation.
67. Almatti Dam
  • Almatti Dam is built on Krishna in Karnataka.
  • It is part of the Upper Krishna Project.
68. Krishna Delta
  • Krishna forms a large delta in Andhra Pradesh.
  • It lies close to the Godavari delta region.
  • The delta supports intensive rice cultivation.
69. Pennar River
  • Pennar is an east-flowing Peninsular river.
  • It is also called Penna.
  • It originates in Karnataka.
  • It flows through Andhra Pradesh.
  • It drains into the Bay of Bengal.
70. North Pennar and South Pennar Trap
  • Pennar/Penna in Andhra Pradesh should not be confused with the South Pennar/Ponnaiyar river system of Tamil Nadu.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Pennar ≠ South Pennar/Ponnaiyar

71. Kaveri River — Overview
  • Kaveri is one of the most important rivers of southern India.
  • It originates in the Western Ghats of Karnataka.
  • It flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
  • It forms a large delta before entering the Bay of Bengal.
  • It is highly important for Tamil Nadu agriculture and water supply.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Kaveri → Major Lifeline of Tamil Nadu

72. Kaveri Source
  • Kaveri originates at Talakaveri.
  • Talakaveri lies in the Brahmagiri Hills of Kodagu district, Karnataka.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kaveri Source → Talakaveri → Brahmagiri Hills → Karnataka

73. Kaveri Course
  • Kaveri flows southeastward from Karnataka into Tamil Nadu.
  • It crosses the Eastern Ghats through a series of gorges and falls.
  • It then enters the Tamil Nadu plains.
  • It forms the fertile Kaveri delta.
74. Major Kaveri Tributaries

Important tributaries include:

  • Hemavati.
  • Harangi.
  • Kabini.
  • Shimsha.
  • Arkavati.
  • Bhavani.
  • Noyyal.
  • Amaravati.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Kaveri Tributaries in Tamil Nadu → Bhavani + Noyyal + Amaravati

75. Kabini River
  • Kabini is an important tributary of Kaveri.
  • It originates in the Western Ghats region.
  • It drains parts of Kerala and Karnataka.
76. Hemavati River
  • Hemavati is an important tributary of Kaveri in Karnataka.
  • It originates in the Western Ghats.
77. Bhavani River
  • Bhavani is one of the major tributaries of Kaveri in Tamil Nadu.
  • It originates in the Western Ghats.
  • It joins Kaveri near Bhavani town.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Bhavani River → Kaveri Tributary

78. Bhavanisagar Dam
  • Bhavanisagar Dam is built across the Bhavani River in Tamil Nadu.
  • It is also known as the Lower Bhavani Project.
  • It is an important irrigation structure.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Bhavanisagar → Bhavani River

79. Noyyal River
  • Noyyal is a tributary of Kaveri.
  • It flows through the Coimbatore and Tiruppur region.
  • It has faced severe pollution from urban and industrial activities.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Noyyal → Coimbatore/Tiruppur

80. Amaravati River
  • Amaravati is an important tributary of Kaveri.
  • It flows through western Tamil Nadu.
  • Amaravathi Dam is built across it.
81. Amaravathi Dam
  • Amaravathi Dam lies in Tiruppur district region of Tamil Nadu.
  • It supports irrigation.
82. Hogenakkal Falls
  • Hogenakkal Falls is located on the Kaveri River in Tamil Nadu.
  • It lies near the Tamil Nadu-Karnataka border region.
  • It is an important physiographic landmark.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Hogenakkal Falls → Kaveri

83. Shivanasamudra Falls
  • Shivanasamudra Falls is located on Kaveri in Karnataka.
  • It is historically associated with early hydroelectric power development in India.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Shivanasamudra → Kaveri → Karnataka

84. Mettur Dam
  • Mettur Dam is built across the Kaveri River in Tamil Nadu.
  • Its reservoir is called Stanley Reservoir.
  • It is one of Tamil Nadu's most important irrigation structures.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Mettur Dam → Kaveri

Reservoir → Stanley Reservoir

85. Mettur Dam Importance

It supports:

  • Kaveri delta irrigation.
  • Water regulation.
  • Hydroelectric power.
  • Regional water supply.
86. Grand Anicut / Kallanai
  • Kallanai is an ancient dam or diversion structure across the Kaveri in Tamil Nadu.
  • It was built during the Chola period.
  • It is traditionally associated with Karikala Chola.
  • It is one of the world's oldest functioning water-diversion structures.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Kallanai → Kaveri → Karikala Chola

87. Location of Kallanai
  • Kallanai lies near Tiruchirappalli.
  • It diverts water into channels that irrigate the Kaveri delta.
88. Kaveri Splitting near Tiruchirappalli
  • Near Tiruchirappalli, Kaveri divides into major channels.
  • The northern branch is called Kollidam/Coleroon.
  • These distributary systems help irrigate the delta.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kaveri Northern Branch → Kollidam/Coleroon

89. Srirangam Island
  • Srirangam lies between the Kaveri and Kollidam rivers near Tiruchirappalli.
  • It is a major river island and cultural centre.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Srirangam → Between Kaveri and Kollidam

90. Kaveri Delta
  • Kaveri delta lies mainly in eastern Tamil Nadu.
  • It is one of the state's most fertile agricultural regions.
  • Paddy cultivation is dominant.
  • The region is often referred to as Tamil Nadu's rice bowl.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Kaveri Delta → Rice Bowl of Tamil Nadu

91. Kaveri Mouth
  • Kaveri reaches the Bay of Bengal through its deltaic distributaries.
  • The historic Poompuhar/Kaveripoompattinam region is associated with the river's coastal outlet.
92. Kaveri Basin States

The basin extends mainly across:

  • Karnataka.
  • Tamil Nadu.
  • Kerala.
  • Puducherry.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Kaveri Basin → Karnataka + Tamil Nadu + Kerala + Puducherry

93. Kaveri Water Importance to Tamil Nadu

Kaveri water supports:

  • Paddy cultivation.
  • Drinking water.
  • Industry.
  • Livestock.
  • Groundwater recharge.
  • Delta ecosystems.
94. South Pennar / Ponnaiyar
  • Ponnaiyar is also known as South Pennar.
  • It originates in Karnataka.
  • It flows through Tamil Nadu.
  • It drains into the Bay of Bengal near Cuddalore region.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Ponnaiyar = South Pennar

95. Ponnaiyar Basin
  • It drains parts of northern Tamil Nadu.
  • Important districts in its broader basin include Krishnagiri, Dharmapuri, Tiruvannamalai, Villupuram and Cuddalore regions.
96. Palar River
  • Palar originates in Karnataka.
  • It flows through Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
  • It reaches the Bay of Bengal along the northern Tamil Nadu coast.
  • Its flow is highly seasonal.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Palar → Highly Seasonal River

97. Palar Water Importance
  • Palar basin groundwater is important for agriculture and domestic supply.
  • Excessive groundwater extraction has created stress in parts of the basin.
98. Cheyyar River
  • Cheyyar is an important tributary of the Palar.
  • It drains parts of northern Tamil Nadu.
99. Vaigai River
  • Vaigai is an important river of southern Tamil Nadu.
  • It originates in the Western Ghats region.
  • It flows through Madurai.
  • It ultimately drains toward the Palk Bay region.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Madurai → Vaigai

100. Vaigai Dam
  • Vaigai Dam is built across the Vaigai River.
  • It is located near Andipatti in Theni district region.
  • It supports irrigation and water supply.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Vaigai Dam → Vaigai River

101. Mullaperiyar and Vaigai Link
  • Water diverted eastward from the Periyar basin through the Mullaperiyar system contributes to the Vaigai basin.
  • This supports agriculture and water supply in southern Tamil Nadu.
102. Tamiraparani River
  • Tamiraparani is an important river of southern Tamil Nadu.
  • It originates in the Western Ghats.
  • It flows mainly through Tirunelveli and Thoothukudi regions.
  • It drains into the Gulf of Mannar.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Tamiraparani → Western Ghats → Gulf of Mannar

103. Tamiraparani Source
  • Tamiraparani originates in the Pothigai/Agasthyamalai Hills of the Western Ghats.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Tamiraparani Source → Pothigai Hills

104. Tamiraparani Tributaries

Important tributaries include:

  • Manimuthar.
  • Gadananathi.
  • Pachaiyar.
  • Chittar.
105. Manimuthar Dam
  • Manimuthar Dam is built on the Manimuthar River.
  • It is an important irrigation project in southern Tamil Nadu.
106. Papanasam Dam
  • Papanasam Dam is associated with the Tamiraparani system.
  • It supports irrigation and hydroelectric power.
107. Tamiraparani Importance
  • Tamiraparani has a relatively dependable flow compared with many Tamil Nadu rivers.
  • Its upper catchment receives substantial rainfall from the Western Ghats.
  • It supports irrigation, drinking water and agriculture.
108. Vellar River
  • Vellar is an east-flowing river system of Tamil Nadu.
  • It drains toward the Bay of Bengal.
  • Several rivers with similar names occur in the state, so location-based questions require care.
109. Vellar and Pichavaram Link
  • The Vellar-Coleroon estuarine region is associated with the Pichavaram mangroves.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Pichavaram → Vellar-Coleroon Region

110. Adyar River
  • Adyar is a short coastal river flowing through Chennai.
  • It drains into the Bay of Bengal.
  • Urbanisation has heavily altered its floodplain and water quality.
111. Cooum River
  • Cooum flows through Chennai.
  • It drains into the Bay of Bengal.
  • It is heavily urbanised and polluted.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Chennai Rivers → Adyar + Cooum

112. Kosasthalaiyar River
  • Kosasthalaiyar is an important river of northern Tamil Nadu.
  • It contributes to the Chennai-region drainage system.
  • It is larger than the Adyar and Cooum systems.
113. Buckingham Canal Link
  • Buckingham Canal runs broadly along parts of the Coromandel Coast.
  • It intersects or connects with several river and backwater systems.
  • It has historical navigation and drainage importance.
114. Subarnarekha River
  • Subarnarekha originates in the Chotanagpur Plateau.
  • It flows through Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha.
  • It drains into the Bay of Bengal.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Subarnarekha → Chotanagpur Plateau

115. Hundru Falls
  • Hundru Falls is located on the Subarnarekha River in Jharkhand.
📌 Must-Memorise

Hundru Falls → Subarnarekha

116. Brahmani River
  • Brahmani is an important east-flowing river of Odisha.
  • It is formed by the confluence of Sankh and South Koel rivers.
  • It drains into the Bay of Bengal.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Brahmani = Sankh + South Koel

117. Baitarani River
  • Baitarani is another important river of Odisha.
  • It originates in the highlands of Odisha.
  • It drains into the Bay of Bengal through a deltaic coastal system.
118. Brahmani-Baitarani Delta
  • Brahmani and Baitarani contribute to an extensive deltaic region in Odisha.
  • The region contains wetlands and mangroves.
119. East-Coast Delta Formation

Large deltas are associated with:

  • Mahanadi.
  • Godavari.
  • Krishna.
  • Kaveri.
📌 Must-Memorise

Major Peninsular Deltas → Mahanadi + Godavari + Krishna + Kaveri

120. Why Peninsular East Rivers Form Deltas
  • They have relatively long courses.
  • They carry sediments across broad plateaus and plains.
  • The east coast has a broad, gently sloping coastal plain.
  • Deposition occurs near river mouths.
121. Why Narmada and Tapi Form Estuaries

Factors include:

  • Rift-valley courses.
  • Narrow western coastal plain.
  • Strong tidal action.
  • Deep river mouths.
  • Reduced large-scale deltaic deposition.
122. Waterfalls in Peninsular Rivers

Important examples include:

  • Jog Falls → Sharavathi.
  • Shivanasamudra → Kaveri.
  • Hogenakkal → Kaveri.
  • Dhuandhar → Narmada.
  • Chitrakote → Indravati.
  • Hundru → Subarnarekha.
📌 TNPSC Favourite

Waterfall ↔ River Matching

  • Srisailam → Krishna.
  • Almatti → Krishna.
  • Mettur → Kaveri.
  • Bhavanisagar → Bhavani.
  • Vaigai Dam → Vaigai.
124. Important City–River Pairings
  • Ahmedabad → Sabarmati.
  • Surat → Tapi.
  • Nashik → Godavari.
  • Hyderabad → Musi.
  • Hampi → Tungabhadra.
  • Madurai → Vaigai.
  • Tiruchirappalli → Kaveri.
  • Chennai → Adyar and Cooum.
125. Peninsular River Basin Agriculture

Major river basins support:

  • Rice.
  • Cotton.
  • Sugarcane.
  • Millets.
  • Pulses.
  • Oilseeds.
  • Horticulture.
126. Irrigation Importance

Peninsular rivers are extensively regulated by:

  • Dams.
  • Barrages.
  • Reservoirs.
  • Canal systems.
  • Tanks.

This is necessary because river discharge is strongly seasonal.

127. Peninsular Rivers and Hydroelectricity
  • Plateau gradients and waterfalls create hydropower opportunities.
  • Western Ghats and major dam sites are especially important.
128. Peninsular Rivers and Floods
  • Although many are seasonal, major east-flowing rivers can produce severe floods during intense monsoon rainfall.
  • Delta regions are particularly vulnerable.
129. Peninsular Rivers and Drought
  • Weak monsoons can sharply reduce reservoir inflows.
  • Drought is especially important in rain-shadow and semi-arid basins.
130. River Pollution

Major pollution sources include:

  • Sewage.
  • Industrial effluents.
  • Agricultural runoff.
  • Sand mining.
  • Solid waste.

Urban rivers such as Noyyal, Cooum and Musi have faced severe pollution problems.

131. Sand Mining
  • Excessive river-sand mining can:
  • Lower riverbeds.
  • Destabilise banks.
  • Damage aquatic habitats.
  • Affect groundwater recharge.
  • Threaten bridges and infrastructure.
132. River Basin Management

Good basin management requires:

  • Water allocation.
  • Pollution control.
  • Flood management.
  • Groundwater conservation.
  • Reservoir operation.
  • Ecosystem protection.
133. Inter-State Rivers

Many Peninsular rivers cross state boundaries.

Examples include:

  • Kaveri.
  • Krishna.
  • Godavari.
  • Narmada.
  • Mahanadi.

Their waters therefore require inter-state coordination.

134. Kaveri Inter-State Geography
  • Kaveri originates in Karnataka.
  • It flows through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
  • Parts of its basin also lie in Kerala and Puducherry.
  • Its water is crucial to both upstream and downstream users.
135. Tamil Nadu River Pattern

Tamil Nadu rivers can broadly be grouped into:

  • Rivers originating in Western Ghats.
  • Rivers entering from neighbouring states.
  • Short east-flowing rivers.
  • Seasonal coastal streams.
136. Why Tamil Nadu Depends on Reservoirs and Tanks

Reasons include:

  • Strongly seasonal rainfall.
  • Many seasonal rivers.
  • Large agricultural demand.
  • High evaporation.
  • Uneven rainfall distribution.
137. Kaveri vs Tamiraparani

Kaveri:

  • Large interstate basin.
  • Major delta.
  • Large irrigation network.

Tamiraparani:

  • Smaller basin.
  • Mostly within Tamil Nadu.
  • Western Ghats source.
  • Relatively dependable flow.
138. Palar vs Vaigai vs Tamiraparani

Palar:

  • Highly seasonal.
  • Northern Tamil Nadu.

Vaigai:

  • Southern Tamil Nadu.
  • Madurai link.

Tamiraparani:

  • Far south.
  • Pothigai source.
  • More dependable.
